newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - up from lows.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - up from lows.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds pared losses in early afternoon trade on Friday, mirroring Treasury bonds, which turned up from lows after a survey of consumer sentiment showed they were a bit less positive in August.
Long municipal bonds, which were marked down an 0.5 in early trade, later were quoted at off 0.2 to unchanged.
Activity was quiet ahead of the summer weekend, as a bid-wanted list with five to six blocks of $10 million each, which was divided among different brokers, failed to produce trades.
"It put some pressure on; it just puts levels in people's heads," a trader explained.
The main gauge of secondary activity, the Standard and Poor's Corp Blue List, stood at $1.35 billion.

Looking ahead to next week, new issues were expected to number 105 and total $1.9 billion. Competitive deals were expected to number 60 and total $682 million, while negotiated deals were seen at 45, totaling $1.2 billion.
In the note market, Texas was expected to offer $2.9 billion of tax and revenue anticipation notes for bids on August 27. The non-callable notes, are dated September 2, 1997 and due August 31, 1998.

Consumer spending accounts for approximately two-thirds of the U.S. economy, and financial market sources said the University of Michigan's preliminary index of consumer sentiment for August fell to 102.8 from 107.1 in the final July report.

Another feature, which helped Treasury bonds trim an early slip, was a bit of a stronger tone seen in the dollar, though it remained below session highs, hurt by concerns Germany might raise interest rates as early as next week.
Both fixed-income and currency markets also were starting to set up for the August 19 meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy making arm.

In Chicago debt futures, the September municipal contracts fell 13 ticks to 119-14/32. The September T-bond contracts slipped six ticks to 113-14/32. The MOB spread slipped about six ticks from levels seen earlier to plus 192 ticks.
In the secondary market, Denver, Colorado, City & County Airport revenue bonds of 2017, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.45 percent, NET, down two basis points.
And Florida Ports Financing Commission Revenues of 2027, which carry a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were offered at 97-1/2, unchanged.
